item.title: The Best-Selling Cards in Disney Lorcana (August 2026)
item.description:
Disney Lorcana|competitive

The Best-Selling Cards in Disney Lorcana (August 2026)

All Vine, All the time.

By Scott Mines

|@HowlingMines
|

Published Sep 4, 2026

|

7 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

The Disney Lorcana North American Championship is in our rear-view mirror and yet another month is sunsetting for the market at large. We're officially in year four for Disney Lorcana. How absurd is that?! I've been writing articles here on TCGplayer since The First Chapter and it doesn't feel even close to that long.

In that time, the Disney Lorcana ecosystem has evolved multiple times. We've seen eras dominated by playables, and others where collectability is king. In fact, it's safe to say that the recent boom in attention has come more so from those big-ticket items. That's led to some speculation that the playability of Disney Lorcana is on a downswing...

...so let me tell you that's utter nonsense. 

I have the pleasure of diving into the numbers here at TCGplayer roughly once a month. Make no mistake: transactions are trending upwards overall, but the majority of those increases can be found in under-$5 must-haves that have rocked a recent tournament. August may have been the biggest example of that in recent memory — not a single card in our top ten currently retails for more than $10 a copy. 

The North American Championship has set the status quo, but the European Championship is quickly coming around the bend. If we see a similar level of commanding performance across the pond, I would expect multiple of these price tags to jump as supply begins to disappear. As a result, it's a good time to be buying in... but what exactly are y'all buying into? 

I've crunched the numbers for you. Let's take a look at the best-selling Disney Lorcana cards throughout August 2026. Spoiler: It's Attack of the Vine! All of the time. 

#10 Lilo & Stitch - Fun-Loving Friends

We said it back when Lilo & Stitch - Fun-Loving Friends was revealed: if Amber Steel is good, you're slamming four copies of this thing. 

Whispers were going around prior to the event, but Joseph Quigley's breakout performance at the North American Championship solidified all doubt of that. Amber Steel is a potent choice if you're looking for counterplay into some of the most popular archetypes in the room right now and Lilo & Stitch are sitting at the helm of that. 

At $2.50? Don't mind if I do. 

#9 Paradise Falls - Exotic Destination

Needless to say, Emerald Steel absolutely dominated at the North American Championship. The deck managed to capture six spots in the top eight and truly stands as the deck to beat right now. The thing is? They've just moved away from the variants of the deck playing Paradise Falls - Exotic Destination. 

Previously, players looked to the location from Attack of the Vine! alongside Touch the Sky in order to draw a fresh fist full of cards. That's still quite powerful, but it's not where you want to be in a room stuffed with both the mirror match and Amber Emerald. 

Will it come back into fashion? Hard to say. I won't pretend it isn't damn cool though. 

#8 Violet Parr - Super Resilient

Honestly, it's a similar story for Violet Parr - Super Resilient. This card had a barnburner of a start to the month as a lynchpin of multiple Amethyst Steel strategies... all of which have begun to underperform as the format has evolved. 

That's not because the card is bad, though. Far from it. Violet is hard to remove and provides potent card selection to any deck capable of shifting her. She's also a spectacular singer for more expensive songs thanks to her shift ability. As a result, I'm fully expecting her to make a comeback as the metagame shifts back in her favor. 

#7 Peter Pan & Tinker Bell - Fast Friends

Ruby Amethyst kind of appeared out of nowhere to steal the CCS $50k Invitational event last month. Garrett Martin prided himself on cooking up a list that had game into Emerald Steel, Amber Emerald and Amber Amethyst — complete with two copies of Peter Pan & Tinker Bell - Fast Friends. 

Playing with (and answering) Evasive characters has quickly become one of the more important aspects of the format and Peter Pan & Tinker Bell - Fast Friends can not only do so itself, but allows any other character to step up to the challenge as well. It also incidentally serves as an activator for Vixey - Expert Fisher and Dumbo - Ninth Wonder of the Universe. 

It's a lot of boxes ticked on a sweet little card. Love it. 

#6 Meilin Lee - Losing Control

I don't think many people are surprised that Meilin Lee - Losing Control has chops. The comparisons to Ariel - Spectacular Singer were not lost on us when she was revealed in Attack of the Vine!. 

That said, I would argue this is still a success story in waiting. While Meilin has seen play in Emerald, Steel and Ruby variants of song decks, none of these have quite managed to break through at the top tournament tables. In my opinion, it's only a matter of time (and maybe a few more cheap songs in Hyperia City) until we really see what she can do. 

#5 Mickey Mouse & Minnie Mouse - Adventuring Duo

Moving onto perhaps the hottest card of the moment: Mickey Mouse & Minnie Mouse - Adventuring Duo have seen most of their sales as a late surge after the North American championship. What's got this tag-team so hot, exactly? 

Well, people really got talking after this Emerald Sapphire deck managed to reach the top eight of a 128-player event. This deck is all about shifting an early copy of Mickey Mouse and Minnie Mouse - Adventuring Duo to quest for buckets of lore, before allowing a near-uncontestable board of Ward characters to sweep up the mess. 

Is it good enough to stick around? I think so. More importantly, the community is snapping up almost every copy they can find at under $3. 

#4 Pocahontas - Guiding the Tribe

Pocahontas is one of the more impressive tools available to the Emerald Amber deck lists featuring Elinor - Renowned Diplomat. After all, what better way to fill out your board the turn before Elinor than dropping bonus extra characters for free?! 

These decks are often pushing 20 one-cost characters, so it's very difficult for Pocahontas - Guiding the Tribe to miss on value before shifting into a back-breaking Pocahontas - Peacekeeper. 

Building a board before protecting it from being challenged? I dunno, that sounds pretty darn good to me. 

#3 Mike Wazowski - Heroic Climber

Speaking of cards that've been earning their keep alongside Elinor, I think we've removed any doubt that Mike Wazowski - Heroic Climber is one of the better early plays in Amber right now. Sure, your opponent has the opportunity to generate card advantage too, but they're not always going to see a character like you will. 

They also can't use any of those cards if you put your foot down and get the game over, so there's that too. 

As far as I'm considered, Mike is one to watch as the format continues to age, and Hyperia City enters the fray. As long as we continue to see a character-heavy aggro deck at the top tables, you'll be seeing plenty of this one on the opposing playmat. 

#2 Gaston - Superior Archer

It's a fall from the throne for Gaston - Superior Archer, who previously held the title as the best-selling card in all of Attack of the Vine!. That said, the fact that Gaston has held onto one of the podium spots since release is one heck of an endorsement for the power level of the card. 

There's plenty of big bads that need to be slain at the top of the format right now, but Gaston really shines in Amber shells packing Support characters like Agustin Madrigal - Exceptionally Kind and Lilo & Stitch - Fun-Loving Friends. In a pinch, you can grant your Support trigger onto an opposing character, giving them enough strength to be brutally struck down. 

This card should be a staple for its entire tenure in Core Constructed, which is still the better part of two years. Grab yourself a foil playset and thank me later. 

#1 Mushu - Stealthy Dragon

Do you know how utterly nuts it is that the most expensive legendary in a set is the best-selling Disney Lorcana card of the month?! It's almost as absurd as the fact that Mushu - Stealthy Dragon is still only sitting at $10 per copy. 

Mushu is one of the fundamental threats of Emerald Steel. It's a must-answer advantage engine that threatens to snowball out of control if left unchecked. I've seen Mushu played in Emerald shells of every color at this stage and I do not expect that to change. To go out on a limb? I think this card is criminally undervalued on account of how many boosters of Attack of the Vine! got opened. 

As we move further from the initial release of the set, that cannot remain true. Mushu has to either fall off in popularity or begin spiralling in price — and I'm putting my money on the latter.

item.title: Five Reasons You Should Be Excited About Levia
item.description:
Flesh and Blood|competitive

Five Reasons You Should Be Excited About Levia

Don't let Viserai and Malice steal the limeline! Karol thinks Levia might be the biggest winner from Usurp the Shadow Throne

By Karol Ruszkiewicz

|

Published Sep 9, 2026

|

5 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

I'm going to be brutally honest: Levia used to be my least favourite hero in the game. But over time, her card pool increased and with Usurp the Shadow Throne, she became one of my favourites. Here's why.

For those who don't know me, I'm a Senior Developer at Legend Story Studios. But before I was a developer, I was a player just like you: playing at my local Armory, driving out to Pro Quests and Skirmishes, and trying to grind some cold foils.

I was fortunate enough to start my journey right after the release of Welcome to Rathe. After a short stint with Bravo, I realised Rhinar was my hero. I loved playing Rhinar so much that I couldn't stop talking about his builds, on podcasts, in articles, pretty much anywhere I could.

Here's a blast from the past from 2020:

Naturally, I considered myself a Brute enjoyer, and I couldn't wait to see what a talented Brute played like.

Then I played Levia.

It just didn't click.

The banishing, the lack of a real hero ability, and the number of hoops you had to jump through with cards like Deep Rooted Evil and Shadow of Blasmophet felt excessive.

Despite enjoying some aspects, like recycling Howl from Beyond and summoning Blasmophet with Doomsday, or blocking with a Carrion Husk, the looming threat of dying to my own hero ability was just too much.

But a lot of that changed with Dusk Till Dawn.

Levia, Consumed is one of my favourite designs in Flesh and Blood. It's a transformational card that can take you down two very different paths while continually pushing your game plan further. Dusk Till Dawn also gave us some really unique designs in the form of Shaden Death Hydra, Slithering Shadowpede and Blood Dripping Frenzy.

A big factor for me was playing towards the hero flip. It could be a bit dicey at times, but having a clear objective to play towards, one based on a precise life total, was incredibly exciting.

Still, some of the fail states were just too punishing for me to fully immerse myself in the Levia experience.

Then came Shadowrealm Horror.

A true reward for perfect graveyard management, and an absolute bomb when played correctly. This was definitely a turning point for me. I started to see Levia as an epic deck that rewards you for walking the fine line on a razor's edge. If you can manage your graveyard, hand and banished zone correctly, the power is there to take on almost any deck in the game.

So, what does Usurp the Shadow Throne have to offer?

1. Gate to i'Arathael

While all the Viserai lovers and new Malice enjoyers swarm towards the spoilers, there's a little secret I want to share with you about gates.

If you think about it, Levia has one of the best ranges of cards to play from the banished zone with them.

A lot of Viserai's cards can already be played from the banished zone and don't need a gate to do it, because why would you play cards that could get stuck there? Meanwhile, Malice mainly focuses on playing out our Corrupted Corpses.

But Levia?

How about that Shadowrealm Horror I just talked about? Or a Mark of the Beast off a blue, just to turn off Blood Debt? Maybe a cheeky Shaden Death Hydra to close out a game?

The possibilities are as wide as you make them.

But most importantly, gates are permanents that act as a failsafe when things aren't going to plan. Before, when you were left with a single card in hand, it could mean having no way to fulfil Blood Debt. Now, thanks to gates, you have a strong bailout mechanism. Simply pitch a blue, play Mark of the Beast, and back to the banished zone it goes.

2. Blasmophet, the Insatiable Hunger

First Doomsday, then Levia, Consumed, and now there's a third Blasmophet to play with!

While it can be just a tad tricky to keep around, if your opponent disrespects it, it's basically an even better Gate to i'Arathael that you have access to every turn.

Cards like Engulfing Shadows, Embraforged Gauntlet and Reach of the Abyss all do an amazing job of keeping the demon from going hungry.

3. Extra Consistency

Gates of iArathael don't just open up crazy power plays - they also increase consistency. But they're not the only cards doing that.

Blood Harvest is a great example of a card that might not look particularly powerful at first glance, but every Brute lover understands the importance of having 6-power blues in the deck to smooth out those Brute-related synergies.

Blood Harvest offers exactly that. It's a one-stop shop for all your Brute needs.

Fulfil Blood Debt? Check.

Act as a pitch card? Check.

Fill up the banished zone for Hexagore? Check.

It's cards like these that can significantly improve the Levia play experience.

4. Brand New Archetypes

Throughout the years, there have been many different Levia builds, constantly evolving as new cards have been released. And this is where I have to give Ethan Van Sant a huge shoutout for relentlessly building, experimenting and rebuilding various Levia decklists over the years.

If you've ever thought of a Levia archetype, chances are Ethan's already tried it.

One of my favourites has always been the combination of Shaden Death Hydra with Tear Limb From Limb - a cheeky combo that can suddenly throw 26 damage at your opponent out of nowhere.

Usurp the Shadow Throne is giving us even more of these unique cards that are bound to create some brand-new combos.

Ingest the Unknown is one of these majestics. Pair that up with a Shaden Death Hydra and you've got yourself the biggest 1-cost attack in the game.

These kinds of interactions feel amazing when you find a way to make them work and this is just the beginning of what's in store.

5. The Best Is Yet to Come

Everything spoiled as of writing this should already be enough to create some brand-new Levia stans. But I have to be honest: the best is still to be revealed.

So stay tuned to the World Premiere stream from September 11th–13th to catch all the latest pieces of the Levia puzzle.

There is at least one card coming that is bound to make your jaw drop and might just convert you into a Levia main.

item.title: The Biggest Price Spikes in Pokémon This Week - 09/09/2026
item.description:
Pokémon|finance

The Biggest Price Spikes in Pokémon This Week - 09/09/2026

Surf(ing Pikachu)'s up.

By Corbin Hosler

|@Chosler
|

Published Sep 9, 2026

|

5 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series: Movers and Shakers

Just one week to go until the release of Pokemon TCG: 30th Celebration—and the market is holding its collective breath.

Once again, overall prices in the weekly window (with a couple of exceptions we'll get to) were mostly flat with no giant gains or drops, including from the recent sets that have been seeing reprints in recent weeks. Instead, the market remains steady as we all prepare for what some expect to be the biggest Pokemon release of 2026.

30th Celebration is releasing in the United States and Japan simultaneously, the first unified release in the Pokémon TCG's history. That's a nice trick to pull for the massive release, and while it may or may not end up as the biggest release ever, it's certainly going to be the biggest since we've entered this ultra-modern era of extreme scarcity and hype cycles.

So hang in there—a week from now you'll be ripping those Futuristic Rare Mew ex and Mewtwo ex. I believe in you.

Let's start this week with Ascended Heroes, which up until now has been the biggest set release of the year and probably the largest since the days of Prismatic Evolutions. It gave us a Gengar that peaked near $1,500, plus different versions of Dragonite and Pikachu that pushed $1,000 as well.

The set blew up in price earlier this summer, but as more supply as finally entered the market (slowly) in recent weeks, we've seen drops almost across the board.

Most of those drops have slowed by now, but a few cards are still trickling down. Mega Gengar ex dipped below $1,000 for the first time in months last week, and it will soon be joined by SIR Pikachu ex 276, which closed this week at an official Market Price of $1,007 but has plenty of live listings in the triple digits rather than quadruple.

SIR Mega Dragonite ex is the other standout from the set, and it's down this week as well. Dragonite once peaked at almost $900 but today is much closer to $600. And SIR Lillie's Clefairy ex is at an all-time low of $155.

Moving on to cards that saw gains this week, once again the most movement came not from ultra-modern sets of the last 1-3 years—remember that not all that long ago, that was where we saw the most movement—but instead from classic sets that may not have caught the market's attention until now.

Like Flying Pikachu, from Rising Rivals. This printing perfectly illustrates the class of card that has been seeing the most movement over the last several weeks: old, but not ancient, and evocative of an already popular Pokemon. It's a tried-and-true formula, and one that continues to pay dividends years later.

Rising Rivals was printed in 2008 and features Snorlax Lv. X most prominently from a set that is extremely scarce by today's standards. In fact, the price on Snorlax is hard to even pin down—there hasn't been a sale of a Near Mint copy in months, and there's none listed on TCGplayer. You're looking at somewhere between $800-$1,000 for even a Lightly Played copy, and Near Mints from that era are very hard to come by today. Alakazam E4 Lv.X spiked from $120 to $300 earlier this year, and even the not-quite-a-reprint Pikachu from the set has sold for $350 multiple times this year.

It's also the set where Pikachu really did it all. Flying Pikachu is climbing most obviously, as supply runs out. Near Mint copies were going for as low as $150 earlier this summer, but after the last copies have sold out, the new price for Flying Pikachu is more like $400 based on live listings.

But Pikachu didn't just fly here—it surfed as well.

Of course this Surfing Pikachu is climbing in price along with the rest of the set. Near Mint copies are somewhere around a cool $1,000, which is more than double what they were selling for earlier this year.

It's really been a big year for Mew, hasn't it? I've written a ton about the reclusive Pokemon this year, and here we have yet another set of Mew printings climbing precipitously in price. It seems it's up there with Pikachu and Charizard and Eeveelutions (Umbreon, it's always Umbreon)—no matter how many times you print a new cool version of the card, the demand exists to eat up copies.

So here we are talking about the XY promo printing of Mew-EX XY126, which along with Mewtwo-EX XY125 came out only as limited-printing bonus cards. That's not uncommon, especially for Mew, and the familiar recipe here led to the same outcome: an expensive Mew that only gets more expensive. In this case, it's up to an all-time high of almost $250, which is double what it was this time a year ago. Mewtwo-EX XY125, meanwhile, is running at around $170 right now.

Everything I said about Rising Rivals also applies to BREAKthrough, the set that released in 2015 and gave us a whole bunch of variant printings of Mewtwo (10, by my count). As crazy as that sounds, they're of course all worth money, ranging from $12 for Mewtwo-EX all the way up to the top end of the micro-Mewtwo market, the reason for our spotlight today.

Mewtwo-EX 164 is the leader of the bunch, and is up this week to over $200 for the first time in its decade-long history. It's been a big climb for this Mewtwo in 2026, which follows up an even stronger 2025. This card was under $50 two years ago, but is pushing up over a $200 Market Price for the first time ever.

Finally, let's look at one of the more fun team-ups in the TCG (although who am I kidding, they're all amazing). Alt-Art Raichu & Alolan Raichu-GX hasn't been cheap in years, but the price today is continuing to push ever higher. While it may not be a giant overnight spike to steal the headlines, this pairing of evolved Pikachus has climbed up to a $360 Market Price—but live listings are even higher, meaning the true updated price of the Raichus is closer to $430.

I'll see you next week for the release of 30th Celebration!

item.title: The Top 10 Bestselling Cards From Yu-Gi-Oh's Magnificent Monsters
item.description:
Yu-Gi-Oh!|finance

The Top 10 Bestselling Cards From Yu-Gi-Oh's Magnificent Monsters

Collectors digging for high-priced cards means competitive players are eating these cards up.

By Zachariah Butler

|

Published Sep 11, 2026

|

5 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series: Bestselling Cards of the Week

One of the most hyped products of the entire year is finally here! Magnificent Monsters combines a lot of solid, tournament-level cards alongside the desired chase of the ever elusive Grand Master Rare cards! These all-new entities in the Yu-Gi-Oh space are shaking up collecting as we know it. Now, there are exceptionally rare cards that come serialized, meaning we can roughly know the exact quantities of each card in the wild!  

That level of scarcity has never been seen before in the game, and seeing anyone pull a Grand Master Rare is a huge privilege. These are worth a life-changing amount of money, with the weakest ones selling for a few thousand, all the way to Dark Magical Curtain selling for over $20,000!

The best part about this though, is that the volume of packs opened means that the core cards are significantly cheaper than they might otherwise be, due to the extremely high amount in circulation. Let's dig right in with the bestsellers from the set though, starting off with a retain of a classic…

The Bestselling Cards From Magnificent Monsters

#10 Crystron Halqifibrax Prism

The successor to Crystron Halqifibrax, Crystron Halqifibrax Prism is an incredibly solid card! While it can't summon any tuner easily, and requires three materials, there will 100 percent be a time we see this card getting abused. Most of the strongest tuners in the current landscape of gameplay are low level anyway, so that's not a real drawback. It's a card that has a ton of application and we will definitely see it getting used sooner or later.  

#9 Ruler of the End of the World  

Demise, King of Armageddon has gotten a massive upgrade and holy smokes it's good! Packing two powerful effects, it both board wipes and can help you cheat out Ritual Monsters with ease at the cost of 2000 life points. It saw some moderate success in the OCG in the hands of various Mitsurugi duelists, since Mitsurugi Ritual is often played as a three-of. At only $1, it's a steal. 

#8 Winged Kuriboh Sabatiel LV10

Jadne Yuki would be so proud to see his little buddy all grown up and searching for Polymerization or Fusion spells at the mere cost of half your life points. Life points aren't a real resource anyway, so it doesn't matter. Once again, fixing the problems in the HERO deck is a difficult task, but Konami keeps finding new ways to approach it. HERO fans are eating good with this set, which is why this is at number eight!  

#7 Synchro Emergency  

Not to be outdone, Yusei Fudo has some new tools in his arsenal as well. Synchro Emergency is one of those cards that just has to be good, right?! Cheating out two monsters for free? That's free real estate. Not only that, but you get to Synchro Summon on the opponent's turn, and we know how good that can be.  

#6 W:P Fancy Ball (Secret Rare)  

I:P Masquerena and S:P Little Knight are combined for terror and holy smokes, W:P Fancy Ball is a terrifying card to behold! Monster effect negation is great. It's also able to use the I:P Masquerena Link Summon effect, using their monsters as well! This is a card that Master Duel players have become accustomed to, much like Promethean Princess, Bestower of Flames, and that's going to be a boon in the coming months.  

#5 Kuriboh – Multiply!  

Kuriboh is better than ever, now it's a turn zero threat. Imagine getting to summon this guy plus any monster with 300 attack and 200 defense from your deck on your opponent's turn. Sounds kind of whatever right? Wrong! Fur Hire has already shown a good finish at the regional level thanks to this card, and the Ritual of Light and Darkness deck can utilize it as well. This is one of the breakout stars from Magnificent Monsters.  

#4 Dark Magical Curtain

The most hyped-up card in Magnificent Monsters by far, Dark Magical Curtain does it all for the Dark Magician deck and does more than that! Special Summoning a Dark Spellcaster is already nice, but getting to search for something like… The Gaze of Timaeus?! That's even better. The real draw though is being able to Special Summon Witch of the Black Forest and search for Droll & Lock Bird when Witch hits the grave, meaning that Droll & Lock Bird interactions are more consistent than they've ever been before.  

#3 Dark Magician, the Pharaoh's Servant  

Another support card for the Dark Magician deck, Dark Magician, the Pharaoh's Servant setting any Spell or Trap card that mentions Dark Magician is already nuts especially when you look at the decks that can use that. Branded, Azamina piles, Ritual of Light and Darkness decks - it's a terrifying array.  

This guy can also just nuke your opponent's backrow at the cost of a single Spell card in your hand, a small price to pay for board breaking these days. Dark Magician, the Pharaoh's Servant is the full package, and he's going to strut his stuff all over your opposition. Dark Magician has already won a Regional Qualifier thanks to it!  

#2 Cyberse Contract Witch  

All roads lead to Habikiri, that's what I'm told. Cyberse Contract Witch was almost immediately broken in the Mitsurugi deck since it takes just two monsters of the same type and discards a Spell card to add any Ritual Monster to your hand. It's going to make Mitsurugi even more consistent, which is a terrifying prospect.  

#1 Favorite HERO Flame Wingman

Another great Super Polymerization target, Favorite HERO Flame Wingman combines Skyscraper with Marauding Captain, both boosting itself by 1000 attack points when facing any monster with 2200 or more attack, and summoning a Level 4 or lower monster from the hand.  

Its second effect is my favorite though, giving you bonus Fusion Summons if a monster died in battle that turn, can we say "efficient OTKs"?!

Looking past the top 10, Number 39: Utopia, Emissary of Light was number 11 barely missing out. Number 12 was Infernal Strike Fighter, a crazy strong OTK card. Number 13 was Gagaga Girl - Cell Phone Subtraction, with number 14 being Gorgon of Zilofthonia, and number 15 was Horoscope Sorcerer, the Stargazer Magician. Magnificent Monsters is a set full of amazing cards and a ton of value, as you can see!

Top 10 Best-Selling MTG Cards of the Week - 09/11/2026

Living in a pauper's paradise.

By Jason Coles

|

Published Sep 11, 2026

|

4 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series: Bestselling Cards of the Week

We're in the midst of Reality Fracture previews after a few months of Universes Beyond, and it turns out that's pretty exciting for us Magic: The Gathering fans. It also turns out that it's nowhere near as big of a deal as the recent changes in Pauper Constructed, which have had an absurdly dramatic effect on this week's best-selling Magic: The Gathering cards. 

Top 10 Best-Selling Magic: The Gathering Cards of the Week - 09/11/2026

A recent Secret Lair reprinted several classic cards with a rarity shift to common, and as a result there are big changes happening in Pauper. All of those are being reflected in this week's list, although a few The Hobbit cards have managed to tough it out and survive the big changes by staying on the list. 

#10 Wizard's Staff

Wizard's Staff is clinging on for dear life here. This two-mana equipment gives the equipped creature prowess and also adds another trigger for any triggered ability. The only limit here is that it's a blue equipment card— otherwise it'd be in every Commander deck ever made. It's just an incredibly strong card. 

#9 Nyxborn Hydra

Nyxborn Hydra is an X and green 0/1 that has reach and trample. It comes in with X +1/+1 counters, but it also has Bestow. For X and two green you can enchant a creature with it, granting it all of those same abilities. It's a very solid card, and it's also a common, making it a pretty heavy-hitting Pauper option. 

#8 Belladonna Took 

Belladonna Took is a mighty two-mana white creature that really loves tokens. You'll gain one life when the first copy enters that turn, then the second copy lets you draw a card, and then the third one lets you put a +1/+1 counter on all of your creatures. This thing makes for an amazing Commander option for mono-white enthusiasts, and is also good in any deck that makes tokens. 

#7 Baleful Strix 

Baleful Strix is the first of a few cards on this list that's now legal in Pauper. It turns out that classic cards suddenly being Pauper-legal will do wonders for how well they're selling. It's not like Baleful Strix really needed another reason to be selling well, but I'm always happy to have it back on one of these lists. 

#6 Soul-Guide Lantern 

Soul-Guide Lantern is a one-mana artifact that lets you exile a card from a library as it enters, then either tap and sacrifice it to exile everyone else's graveyard, or pay one and sac it to draw a card. All good options for sure, especially now that it's legal in Pauper. That's a big leap in how playable this classic card is. 

#5 Flora Colossus

Flora Colossus is a big old seven-mana X/X with hexproof. Its power and toughness are the same as the number of lands you control, and it makes for an extraordinarily good end-game option for big stompy decks that can give this thing trample. There are a few land synergies already showing up in Reality Fracture previews, so it's only natural that this would be doing well. 

#4 Thraben Charm 

Thraben Charm is a two-mana white instant that lets you deal a bunch of damage to a target creature, destroy an enchantment, or exile some graveyards. These are all good effects in pretty much any format, and having them all on one card is amazing. It's a very flexible answer to plenty of problems, and is selling well because of Pauper and Commander. 

#3 Full Art Middle-earth Basic Lands

Order has been restored, and The Hobbit Full Art Lands are back together again. This week the Mountain is heading up the group, although the first isn't too far behind. The Plains, Swamp, and Island only just sneak in at all actually. Still, they're very pretty lands, and they'll keep selling well until we get whatever cool artwork Reality Fracture is offering. 

#2 Giant's Boulder

Giant's Boulder has slipped a little this week, but remains a very sought-after card. This one-mana artifact lets you scry 2 as it enters, lets you pay one mana and tap it for one mana of any color, or you can pay seven and sacrifice it to destroy a permanent of your choice. It's just a strong all-rounder, and it's also Pauper-legal. 

#1 Dispatch

Dispatch has been selling obscenely well, actually beating out second place by nearly 400%, all because it's legal in Pauper now. As you've seen with a few other entries, the big changes to Pauper have had a massive difference, so it makes sense. This one-mana white instant taps a creature normally, but with three artifacts or more in play it exiles the creature instead. It's excellent removal, and it's a must-have now.

item.title: The Biggest One Piece Card Price Shifts in August 2026
item.description:
One Piece|finance

The Biggest One Piece Card Price Shifts in August 2026

OP-17 had some unexpected winners.

By Anthony Tachella

|@tinymech
|

Published Sep 11, 2026

|

6 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

August was an interesting month for the One Piece Card Game. The game is now finally set on a unified release schedule, meaning that the Eastern and Western formats are finally combined! 

Now that we aren't separated by a 3+ month gap from Japan, the game is in a wild zone at the start of each format. We don't have tournament experience overseas to influence our metagame or market shifts. 

Because of this craziness, we're seeing all sorts of changes in the market. Less influenced by collectors and more by the competitive player base. 

Red and Black Straw Hats

The newest wave of Starter Decks featured amazing support for Red Straw Hat decks. When combined with the new Black Straw Hat support in OP-17, you have an amazing Straw Hat Sabo strategy that utilizes the awesome new Elbaph cards.

First of all, let's look at the ST-01 Brook! This is one of the 15 cards that were given an updated block number. So, even though pretty much every print of it says Block 1, it is considered to be Block 4 for legality's sake. This card has always been a solid Red Straw Hat card because of its +2000 Counter along with a solid On Play effect.

Because the Straw Hat strategy is so strong in Red and Red/Black, Brook has been going up like crazy in pretty much every printing. The original common from ST-01 is almost $5 now! At the start of August it was sitting around a quarter, so that's a huge jump. The Pirate Foil printing from PRB-02 is in a similar situation as well. It has gone from less than a dollar to around $4 on average in just a month. 

Premium versions of this Brook are also going up in value, with the Tournament Pack and Premium Card Collection printings creeping up in price. The Premium Card Collection printing is probably my favorite one; it has the realistic artwork of Brook in his Soul King persona and is textured to boot! This version is currently sitting around $22, a little more than double what it was a month ago.

There are two Black Straw Hat cards that have certainly spiked in price in the last month. The first one we're going to talk about is Pirates Docking Six from OP-15. This card was originally printed as support for the Brook deck, but has quickly become a staple card in any Black Straw Hat strategy. 

Black colored decks often are themed around using the Trash as an additional resource. This card is awesome for that! It gives you extra cards in the Trash while bringing out a character from the Trash. The biggest perk of this card is its continuous effect. The fact that it is an 11-cost card on the field is huge. This automatically makes OP-13 Sabo's Leader effect live. Which gives a +1000 boost to your whole field. This is a huge buff for the deck, even if you don't have the right cost on the field for your Elbaph characters, you can still boost their power with your Leader effect. This card shot up to $9 for a hot minute, but has since stabilized around the $7 mark recently, which isn't a huge dip, but it feels good to see a Rare dropping in price like this. 

The Thousand Sunny from ST-14, however, can perfectly complement Pirates Docking Six and make it a 12-cost card on the field. Giving all of your characters +1 cost is incredibly strong. Even if it isn't really used in OP-13 Sabo, it is used in the Elbaph Luffy deck that premiered with OP-17. This card shot up to almost $5 in the last month! 

Purple Ramps and Green Fishes

Purple and Green have both gotten their fair share of support recently in the competitive sense. On the Purple Side, we have the new support for Animal Kingdom and Big Mom Pirates. OP-17 Kaido and OP-11 Charlotte Katakuri are both really fun strategies and have caused plenty of cards to shoot up in price.

Let's start with EB-04 Queen, released for us in the OP-14/EB-04 set. This new Queen is essential to the new Kaido deck, since it gives an easy recurring ramping effect that you can use multiple times. Because of the new Kaido deck, Queen has shot up to almost $4 a copy. I'm honestly surprised it isn't more, considering it comes from a larger booster set and is a little harder to pull because of it. 

We also have the OP-11 Charlotte Pudding, which used to be a bulk SR, now sitting around the $6 mark! This is your main searcher in Purple Big Mom Pirates decks. Purple Big Mom Pirates decks are getting more popular, with both Katakuri and Pudding Leaders being viable options for the decks. The Alternate Art for Pudding has also been going up quite a bit over the last month. At the start of August, the alt art Pudding was sitting around $15, and now it is closer to $30! This is a huge jump for an SR that hasn't seen a lot of competitive play.

Alright, one of the most hyped up decks right now is the Green Mihawk deck that utilizes the new 10-cost Shanks from OP-17. Resting your opponent's field is strong; getting 2 Don back when you do so is even stronger. So what do you do with those 2 Don? Play Vander Decken IX to KO any Character your opponent controls! 

Being able to KO anything, even a 10-cost character, at the cost of a Fish-Man Character from hand is insane. It has single-handedly caused cards like OP12-023 Kawamatsu to shoot up in price. Pretty much every Green deck is playing Shanks right now, so every Green deck is playing Vander Decken and Kawamatsu to make sure they have enough Fish-Man cards to discard to clean up the opponent's field. 

Nico Robin Takes The Spotlight

One of the strongest Leaders right now in the competitive scene is OP-09 Nico Robin, which recently got a huge boost from all the Yellow Big Mom Pirates support in OP-17. The crazy thing about all of these new Yellow cards is that they aren't locked to a specific Leader or Leader Type. Meaning that every Yellow deck can play them! 

Nico Robin is one of the coolest Yellow Leaders because she has Banish and she has access to Gum-Gum Giant. Banish is a crazy powerful ability in a format where hand advantage is everything. Since those Life cards never end up in the opponent's hand, you're constantly putting more pressure on your opponent.

As for Gum-Gum Giant? That's still just one of the strongest cards in the game. Hands down. Sure, you have to go -2 on your Don, but with how much this deck can ramp, you don't even mind. 

The Alt Art Nico Robin Leader has jumped up from around the $70 mark to almost $160 in the last month! Both the competitive side of the game and Robin being a fan-favorite character are to blame for this huge price spike. 

This has been an interesting month for the One Piece Card Game's market. With a ton of cards rising in price, those who hold onto their bulk are rejoicing. While we only looked at price spikes, there are still cards that have dropped a ton in value recently. All of the Round1 promos have tanked in value, but that's also because of the fourth wave of their release. With more waves of releases on the way, the Round1 promos should continue to dip in price until they're a little more reasonable.

item.title: Collector's Guide to Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration
item.description:
Pokémon|collecting

Collector's Guide to Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration

From Classic Collection to Futuristic Rare.

By Peter Day

|

Published Sep 11, 2026

|

4 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

The wait is almost over!

The Pokémon Company is commemorating the 30th anniversary of their TCG with what might be its most hyped Pokémon expansion of all time. Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration officially releases worldwide on September 16, 2026, bringing two brand-new rarities, loads of alternate-art cards to collect, and reprints of some of the most iconic cards in the history of the game.

There's so much to explore in the biggest Pokémon set of 2026—so we've drawn you a map. Here are all the kinds of cards you might find in a booster pack of 30th Celebration, roughly ordered from least to most rare.

Energy Cards

Every 30th Celebration booster pack comes with one of eight foil Energy cards numbered 009 through 016. These cards are illustrated by YOSHIROTTEN, in the same style as the Futuristic Rare cards that will be some of the biggest chases in 30th Celebration.

Main Set Cards

Energy cards aside, there are 188 cards in 30th Celebration, which can be divided into three categories: 128 mechanically unique main set cards, 30 parallel Secret Rare cards, and 30 reprints of historic cards called the Classic Collection.

30th Celebration's main set consists of 128 cards at four rarities: Common, Rare, Double Rare, and the new Pikachu Rare rarity. (There are no Uncommons in 30th Celebration.)

68 Commons and 18 Rares

  • Rarity Symbol (Commons): Black Circle.
  • Rarity Symbol (Rares): Black Star.

Commons and Rares are the most common type of card you'll find in 30th Celebration packs.

Unlike other Pokémon sets, both Rares and Commons in 30th Celebration are always foil. There are no Reverse-Holo variants of any cards in 30th Celebration.

12 Double Rares

  • Rarity Symbol: Two Black Stars.

All the Double Rares in 30th Celebration are normal-version Pokémon ex.

30 Pikachu Rares

  • Rarity Symbol: ##/30.

The fifth card in every 30th Celebration pack is always one of 30 different Pikachu cards with unique art and game text. Instead of a rarity symbol, these Pikachu have a number out of 30 (e.g. 16/30) in addition to their normal collector number.

Many collectors will start their 30th Celebration journey by trying to complete a set of these Pikachu Rares, which will make all of them more valuable by association. In the short-term though, the most popular one might be OKACHEKE's Pikachu 14/30 with its face squished between the balusters, which fans fell in love with early in the set's preview season.

Secret Rare Cards

There are 30 Secret Rare cards in 30th Celebration, numbered 129/128 through 158/128. These Secret Rares are all full-card alternate-art versions of cards from the 30th Celebration main set.

18 Illustration Rares

  • Rarity Symbol: Gold Star

Eighteen of the Common and Rare cards in the 30th Celebration Main Set have a parallel Illustration Rare version, numbered 129/128 through 146/128.

The most valuable Illustration Rares in 30th Celebration will likely be the three legendary birds, both because of their enduring popularity and because their three cards link together to form one connected piece of artwork.

10 Special Illustration Rares

  • Rarity Symbol: Two Gold Stars

It is believed that 10 of the Double Rare cards in the 30th Celebration Main Set have a parallel Special Illustration Rare version, numbered 147/128 through 156/128.

The most valuable Special Illustration Rares in 30th Celebration will likely be the Day and Night Pikachu ex cards, which feature cameos by the other Pokémon who appear in the set.

2 Futuristic Rares

  • Rarity Symbol: Turquoise Star.

30th Celebration includes two cards with a new rarity called Futuristic Rare: Mew ex and Mewtwo ex. Both of these cards are illustrated by renowned Japanese artist YOSHIROTTEN, who developed the look for the rarity inspired by themes from his 2018 FUTURE NATURE exhibition.

Because of their special rarity, these will likely be the most valuable cards in 30th Celebration. Of the two, Mew ex will likely be more expensive than Mewtwo ex due to its competitive potential if nothing else. Players hope Mew ex's Memory Helix Ability will offer a new way to counter the Dragapult ex deck, which has been dominating Standard for months and just won the 2026 World Championships.

30 Classic Collection Cards

  • Rarity Symbol: Varies.

30th Celebration also includes a subset of 30 iconic cards from the history of the Pokémon TCG called the Classic Collection. These cards are reprinted exactly as they were in their original sets (including their original rarity symbol and set number), and are only distinguishable by their 30th Anniversary logo.

Like Secret Rares, Classic Collection cards can sometimes be found in 30th Celebration booster packs. In addition, the 30th Celebration Ultra-Premium Collection (Day) and (Night) products that release on November 6 will each come with one Classic Collection booster pack containing three cards from this subset.

Pokémon's 25th Anniversary set, Celebrations, also featured a Classic Collection subset. If precedent is any indication, we expect the new reprint of Base Set Charizard to be the most popular and valuable card from the 30th Celebration Classic Collection.

Depending on how the pull rates of Futuristic Rares and Classic Collection cards compare to each other, Classic Collection Charizard might come out ahead of Futuristic Rare Mew ex as the most expensive card in all of 30th Celebration.
